newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed, budget deal helps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed, budget deal helps.

text.p: U.S. stocks traded in London were mixed to slightly firmer on Tuesday, with some sectors benefiting from an historic budget and tax deal ironed out by President Clinton and Republican leaders late on Monday, traders said.
The Dow industrials were expected to open five to 10 points higher after finishing at 8,121.11 yesterday when they touched a record high of 8,178.01.
Yet traders said they were cautious before the U.S. employment cost index for the second quarter, due out at 1230 GMT, and July unemployment data that will be reported on Friday.

Shares in Philip Morris Cos Inc rose to $45 from $44-7/8 in New York, traders said, on a favourable response to the accord to balance the U.S. federal budget and cut taxes by $90 billion over the next five years.
A Republican source said U.S. cigarette taxes will increase by up to 15 cents a pack over the next five years. The federal tax is now 24 cents per pack of 20 cigarettes.
Archer Daniels Midland Co also benefited from the tax deal which will leave the ethanol subsidy unchanged, traders said. ADM shares rose $1/8 to $22-1/2.
A possible U.S. government probe hurt shares in United Technologies Corp, which fell 3/8 to $84-1/8, traders said.
The company said on Monday it believed that, in light of the current government contracting environment, it would be the subject of one or more government investigations.
Traders said Cyrix Corp stock jumped $2-1/2 to about $25-1/2 after National Semiconductor said it agreed to buy Cyrix in a stock deal valued at $550 million.
National Semi shares fell to $32-5/8 from $33 in New York.
Trading was still quiet before the economic data.
The cost index, or ECI, is forecast to rise 0.8 percent on the quarter after a 0.6 percent increase in the first quarter, according to a Reuters survey.
Also due out on Tuesday was the July consumer confidence index, at 1400 GMT, and the Redbook Retail Sales Index for the week ending July 26, at 1855 GMT.
"It is getting into the summer doldrums but we've got a lot of numbers," one trader said. "And today's employment cost index is getting more and more attention."
At 1100 GMT, the September S&P futures on GLOBEX were trading 1.05 points higher at 944.70 and the September long bond was up 5/32 at 115-19/32.
